**TREASURY LEGISLATIVE AFFAIRS — MORNING BRIEF**
*Public-source prototype. Not an official product.*

---

**TOP LINE**
Two competing Senate budget resolutions (S.Con.Res. 38, S.Con.Res. 39) sit on the Legislative Calendar with ten-year revenue, debt, and reconciliation instructions that directly bind Treasury's borrowing authority and tax policy agenda. The continuing resolution landscape is active: H.R. 6500 is in Senate-to-House message status and H.R. 9770 has been received in the Senate. Funding gaps at either stage create operational risk for IRS and Fiscal Service.

**NOMINATIONS**
Gadwood (IRS Chief Counsel) referred at 57 days. Kothari (Assistant Secretary) returned at 228 days. Korb (IRS Chief Counsel) and Trennert and Petit (Assistant Secretaries) all withdrawn after extended delays. IRS Chief Counsel vacancy remains a priority gap.

**LEGISLATION AND RULES**
FinCEN published a revised Beneficial Ownership Information Reporting rule (Aug. 14) and issued a Minnesota Geographic Targeting Order (Aug. 11). IRS finalized backup withholding guidance on third-party network transactions (Aug. 10). Two FIO elimination bills (H.R. 643, S. 5158) are active in both chambers.

**HEARINGS**
House Financial Services Subcommittee holds FinCEN oversight hearing; Director Andrea Gacki testifies.

**TOP LINE**
H.R. 7147 became P.L. 119-86, extending FY2026 continuing appropriations. Funding levels remain below operational baseline, sustaining execution risk for IRS filing-season readiness and debt management. FinCEN's beneficial ownership reporting revision published Aug. 14 and a Minnesota geographic targeting order published Aug. 11 are active implementation priorities.

**NOMINATIONS**
Gadwood (IRS Chief Counsel) referred, pending 56 days. Kothari (Assistant Secretary) returned after 227 days. Korb (IRS Chief Counsel), Trennert, and Petit withdrawn after extended holds. IRS Chief Counsel vacancy remains unresolved.

**LEGISLATION & RULES**
Ways and Means received three bills: H.R. 10090 (excise tax on higher education institutions over athletic participation), H.R. 10060 (mandatory presidential audit), and H.R. 10049 (VITAL Act housing tax credit). H.R. 10044 AI Tax and Work Protection Act referred jointly to Ways and Means. Backup withholding rule on third-party network transactions published Aug. 10.

**HEARINGS**
House Financial Services Subcommittee scheduled oversight hearing on FinCEN. Director Andrea Gacki is the sole witness. Staff should prepare members on BOI reporting revision and GTO activity.

**TREASURY LEGISLATIVE AFFAIRS — MORNING HILL BRIEF**
*Public-source prototype. Not an official product.*

---

**TOP LINE**
FinCEN Director Gacki testifies today before House Financial Services. The Beneficial Ownership Information reporting revision rule (pub. Aug. 14) will likely draw questions. Treasury should anticipate oversight pressure on BOI implementation timelines and enforcement posture.

---

**NOMINATIONS**
IRS Chief Counsel nominee Gadwood remains in committee (55 days). Kothari (Asst. Secretary) was returned after 226 days. Korb (IRS Chief Counsel) and Trennert and Petit (Asst. Secretaries) were all withdrawn. Two IRS Chief Counsel slots have now cycled without confirmation.

---

**LEGISLATION & RULES**
Ways and Means activity is heavy. Key bills to track: H.R. 10104 (dyed fuel penalty repeal, Highway Trust Fund revenue risk); H.R. 10060 (presidential audit mandate, IRS independence and resources); H.R. 9801 (ABLE MATCH, Section 529A fiscal exposure); H.R. 10044 (AI tax provisions, novel classification questions). GTO targeting Minnesota financial institutions published Aug. 11. Backup withholding rule on third-party networks published Aug. 10.

---

**HEARINGS**
House Financial Services Subcommittee: Oversight of FinCEN. Witness: Director Andrea Gacki.

**TREASURY HILL BRIEF**
*Public-source prototype — not an official product*
**[DATE]**

---

**TOP LINE**
FinCEN Director Gacki testifies before House Financial Services today. FinCEN's BOI reporting rule published August 14 and a Minnesota geographic targeting order published August 11 will likely draw member questions on compliance scope and small-business burden.

---

**NOMINATIONS**
IRS Chief Counsel nominee Gadwood was referred to the full Senate at day 54. Prior nominees Kothari (Asst. Secretary, 225d) and Korb (IRS Chief Counsel, 271d) were returned or withdrawn. Three additional Asst. Secretary slots remain unfilled after withdrawals.

---

**LEGISLATION & RULES**
H.R. 10104 would eliminate dyed-fuel excise penalties, risking trust fund revenue erosion. H.R. 10090 imposes a new college athletics excise tax with significant IRS implementation burden. H.R. 9801 expands ABLE account matching under IRC 529A. H.R. 7147 is now Public Law 119-86; Treasury should confirm IRS and Fiscal Service funding continuity. Backup withholding rules on third-party network transactions published August 10.

---

**HEARINGS**
House Financial Services Subcommittee: Oversight of FinCEN. Witness: Director Andrea Gacki.

**TREASURY LEGISLATIVE AFFAIRS — MORNING BRIEF**
*Public-source prototype. Not an official product.*

---

**TOP LINE**
FinCEN Director Gacki testifies today before House Financial Services. The BOI reporting requirement revision published August 14 remains the highest-visibility active rulemaking. H.R. 7147 is now Public Law 119-86, providing continuing appropriations for Treasury operations including IRS.

---

**NOMINATIONS**
Gadwood (IRS Chief Counsel) was referred to the full Senate at day 53. Kothari (Assistant Secretary) was returned after 224 days. Korb (IRS Chief Counsel) and Trennert and Petit (both Assistant Secretary) were withdrawn after 270, 381, and 550 days respectively. IRS Chief Counsel vacancy remains unresolved.

---

**LEGISLATION AND RULES**
Active bills of note: H.R. 10104 eliminates dyed-fuel penalties, creating excise tax revenue and compliance risk. H.R. 10090 imposes a new IRS-administered excise tax on higher education institutions. H.R. 9801 creates ABLE account matching contributions requiring IRS design and SSA coordination. The BOI revision and Minnesota geographic targeting order require near-term monitoring.

---

**HEARINGS**
House Financial Services Subcommittee: Oversight of FinCEN. Witness: Director Andrea Gacki.

**TOP LINE**
H.R. 6500, the FY2027 continuing resolution, passed the Senate and returns to the House. Treasury's Fiscal Service and debt issuance operations remain exposed until enactment. H.R. 8595 and H.R. 9770, both received in the Senate, carry appropriations for TFI/OFAC and core departmental offices including IRS and FinCEN. Funding gaps across any of these vehicles would impair sanctions enforcement, tax administration, and cash management functions.

**NOMINATIONS**
Gadwood (IRS Chief Counsel) was referred to the full Senate at day 52. Four nominations remain stalled or cleared: Kothari returned at day 223; Korb and Trennert withdrawn at days 269 and 380 respectively; Petit withdrawn at day 549. IRS Chief Counsel and two Assistant Secretary slots remain unfilled.

**LEGISLATION & RULES**
Senate Finance received S. 5227 (First-Time Homebuyer) and S. 5216 (Senior Accessible Housing Tax Credit); House companions H.R. 7468 and H.R. 9554 also active. S. 3333 (Emergency Savings Enhancement) calendared in the Senate. All engage IRS administration and OTP scoring. FinCEN published a Geographic Targeting Order for Minnesota (Aug. 11). Backup withholding rules on third-party network transactions published Aug. 10.

**HEARINGS**
House Financial Services Subcommittee: FinCEN oversight hearing, witness Director Andrea Gacki.
